Apple has today accused a new UK proposal targeting App Store fees of amounting to price regulation, warning it could harm innovation and investment. Full details below.

Apple Fights Back Against UK App Store Regulation

According to Reuters, Apple today filed a formal response to a consultation by the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), opposing a proposed rule that would allow app developers to link to alternative payment methods.

The CMA gained the ability to impose such requirements after designating both Apple and Google as having "strategic market status" in their respective mobile platform markets last year. Under the UK's new digital markets regime, this designation allows the regulator to introduce company-specific rules aimed at promoting competition and giving consumers more choice.

Under the proposal, Apple and Google could still take a commission on transactions completed by developers through other payment methods, but any such fees would have to be deemed "fair and reasonable".

Reuters noted that the CMA "expects referral fees to be lower than current App Store rates, with the savings passed on to UK consumers or reinvested in developers' businesses to support innovation".

Apple, however, disagrees and has objected to the proposal. Here's the Reuters report:

The CMA rejected Apple's characterisation of the move as price regulation, stating it is designed to establish principles for determining whether referral fees are fair and reasonable, rather than directly setting fee levels.
